body:
# Independent audit: a compact full-shape intrinsic lift over the original integer bases



The dependence components and finite-row offset construction are those in `candidate dbf3b23d25004153`. This audit checks the proposed strengthening that keeps the original coarse integer bases and puts the extra graph coordinates in continuous space.

## 1. Precise retained-family hypotheses

Let P be a fixed finite nonempty lattice-convex subset of Z^k. Initially assume aff(P)=R^k. For each l let K_(l,z), z in P, be full-dimensional compact convex bodies in R^m, satisfying every anchored compatibility inclusion

    sum_z lambda_z K_(l,z) subset K_(l,j)
    whenever j=sum_z lambda_z z belongs to P.

Let M_l>0 be a common normalizer, and suppose

    |K_(l,z)|/M_l -> p_z>0  for every z in P,
    sum_z |K_(l,z)|/M_l <= C.

In the intended application M_l is the total original coarse mass, P consists of the indices with positive limiting relative mass, and C=1. The positive support P is lattice-convex by actual compatibility and Brunn--Minkowski. Its hull has precisely the retained original fibers: it contains each such fiber, is contained in the original body, and its integer projection is P. Thus deletion introduces no new integer fiber.

If the deleted original mass is o(M_l), the retained mass ratio tends to one. This statement concerns a fixed finite original coarse support, or an independently proved negligible discarded mass; positive weights on a named finite subset alone do not establish negligible deletion.

Let P_1,...,P_s be the dependence components. Every anchored representation with more than one distinct source has its target and all positive-coefficient sources in one component. Let L(P) be the scalar functions preserving all these representations. It is the direct sum of the component spaces, and every component indicator chi_i=1_(P_i) belongs to L(P).

## 2. Common-volume normalizations and bounded offsets

For each component i choose a linear map T_(l,i) with

    det T_(l,i)=1/M_l>0.

These maps can be chosen so that the diameters of all transformed component fibers are bounded uniformly in l. Indeed, normalize one anchor by a maximal-simplex map at the prescribed determinant. The anchor's normalized volume stays between positive constants. The fixed finite anchored representations propagate diameter bounds through the component, as proved in Section 3 of the dependence-components note. All normalized volumes lie in a common interval [v,V] with v>0. Translations of the anchor are irrelevant to this diameter argument.

Write K'_(l,z)=T_(l,i)K_(l,z) for z in P_i. These are still compatible, since every nontrivial anchored relation stays within one component. Their centroids c_(l,z) satisfy bounded defects for every row of the finite anchored-representation matrix A:

    |c_(l,j)-sum_z lambda_z c_(l,z)| <= D.

Both points belong to K'_(l,j). Project c_l orthogonally onto ker(A) tensor R^m=L(P) tensor R^m, obtaining g_l. A fixed right inverse on the row space gives uniformly bounded c_l-g_l. Hence

    R_(l,z)=T_(l,i)K_(l,z)-g_(l,z)

are contained in a common ball, preserve all anchored inclusions exactly, and have volumes |K_(l,z)|/M_l.

The original-coordinate offsets

    h_(l,z)=T_(l,i)^(-1)g_(l,z),  z in P_i,

also lie in L(P) tensor R^m. This is an essential check: the inverse map varies by component, but every row of A is supported in just one component. Therefore no relation is violated by these componentwise inverse maps. Component-constant terms require no separate exception; they are already in L(P).

## 3. Exact lift, actual integer fibers, and full affine dimension

Choose a basis

    1, z_1,...,z_k, G_1,...,G_t

of L(P), and put G(z)=(G_1(z),...,G_t(z)). Use s mutually orthogonal copies of R^m and an orthogonal R^t feature block. The enlarged continuous dimension is D=sm+t. Define the fiber

    F_(l,z)={(e_i tensor x,G(z)): x in R_(l,z)}, z in P_i,

and the convex hull

    C_l^lift=conv union_(z in P) ({z} times F_(l,z)).

Every integer fiber of this hull is exactly the displayed F_(l,z). Its projection has integer points precisely P. Any convex representation of an integer base j uses sources in its own dependence component, unless it is the trivial source j. The block-coordinate Minkowski average therefore lies in R_(l,j), and the feature coordinate is exactly G(j), by its defining membership in L(P). Conversely the displayed fiber was included in the hull. This proves both containments, including representations that use j itself.

Each actual integer fiber has intrinsic dimension exactly m, and its embedding is an isometry of R^m. Consequently

    H_m(F_(l,z))=|R_(l,z)|=|K_(l,z)|/M_l.

There is no hidden graph-slope factor: z and G(z) are fixed on a fiber, and only its orthogonal m-block varies.

The hull C_l^lift is already full-dimensional in R^k times R^D. Each full m-dimensional fiber supplies all directions in its own block. After quotienting by these sm block directions, the projected graph (z,G(z)) has affine span k+t, because the displayed functions form a basis. Thus the total affine dimension is sm+k+t=k+D. In particular the fact that the integer fibers have dimension m<D does not make the ambient convex hull lower-dimensional.

If the original P has affine rank k<n, first identify its saturated affine lattice aff(P) intersect Z^n with Z^k by an integer affine change of base coordinates. This preserves counting on the bases and leaves all continuous fiber metrics unchanged. Then apply the preceding construction. No continuous metric distortion is needed for this base-rank reduction.

The case m=0 is excluded from the determinant normalization: det on R^0 is one, and H_0 counting masses cannot be rescaled by this construction.

## 4. One global affine pullback and exact measure identity

Since h_l lies in L(P) tensor R^m, there is an affine vector-valued function H_l(z,g) such that H_l(z,G(z))=h_(l,z). Define the global affine map

    A_l(z,X_1,...,X_s,g)
      =(z, sum_i T_(l,i)^(-1)X_i + H_l(z,g)).

On the fiber over z in P_i this is x -> T_(l,i)^(-1)(x+g_(l,z)), precisely recovering K_(l,z). Its m-dimensional Jacobian there is det T_(l,i)^(-1)=M_l. Therefore, for the unnormalized lifted intrinsic measure nu_l,

    (A_l)_# nu_l = mu_l^retained/M_l.

This is a source-measure identity, not a D-dimensional ambient Jacobian formula. The affine map may be noninjective away from the source.

Every closed original halfspace containing the image of a lifted source point pulls back to a closed affine halfspace containing that point, or to the entire space. Empty pullbacks cannot contain the point. Thus, writing rho_l=mu_l^retained(total)/M_l when M_l is the original total mass,

    depth_original(A_l(y)) >= rho_l depth_lift(y).

All oblique original normals are included, even when the coefficients of A_l diverge with l. No convergence of those affine maps is required.

## 5. Residual total variation and the cross-block continuity issue

Pass to a simultaneous Hausdorff subsequence R_(l,z)->R_(*,z). The limiting volumes are p_z>0, so all residual limits remain full m-dimensional bodies. Convex-body indicators converge in L1 in each fixed m-block. There are finitely many fixed affine source planes, hence

    ||nu_l-nu_*||_TV -> 0.

The limit fibers preserve all anchored inclusions and have exactly the same intrinsic dimensions and integer indices. The limit hull is again full-dimensional by the same graph-span argument.

A direct common-normal slab argument across all s blocks would be invalid: an original cap can be constant on another block. The correct repair is component isolation.

Each chi_i is an affine function of (z,G). Let L be any affine halfspace functional on the lifted ambient space. The functional

    L-Q(1-chi_i)

agrees with L on component i. Since every other source fiber is compact, for a sufficiently large finite Q it is strictly negative on all other components. Thus every component-i cut extends to a global cut excluding all other source components. Conversely any global cut retains at least its component-i mass. It follows exactly, for y in component i, that

    depth_lift(y) = (nu_l(component i)/nu_l(total))
                    depth_(component i)(y).

Within a component, all variable source coordinates occupy the SAME m-block; features and bases are fixed on each fiber. If all residual bodies lie in R B_m, moving a candidate by delta within its source plane changes every through-candidate threshold in that component by at most |u_i| |delta|. For u_i nonzero divide by |u_i| and bound each slab by kappa_(m-1)R^(m-1)|delta|. For u_i=0 the cap is unchanged. Therefore the normalized component depth is Lipschitz with constant

    |P_i| kappa_(m-1) R^(m-1)/nu_l(component i).

These constants are uniformly bounded. This argument works also for m=1 with kappa_0=1. Closed supporting boundaries carry no m-volume when the block normal is nonzero; block-normal-zero cuts are exactly unchanged.

Combining this Lipschitz estimate with Hausdorff candidate recovery and total-variation convergence proves convergence of each component maximum, and therefore

    max depth_lift,l -> max depth_lift,*.

For example, the same-center comparison uses the uniform TV bound over all halfspaces; moving to a nearest point in the approximating fiber then costs at most the displayed Lipschitz constant times its Hausdorff error. Applying this in both directions proves the assertion and does not rely on Portmanteau at a charged boundary plane.

If rho_l->1, the exact pullback inequality finally gives

    liminf_l max depth_original,l >= max depth_lift,*.

This is a valid lower-semicontinuous depth transfer retaining complete residual bodies. It does not identify the depth of a projected weak limit, discard transverse cap information, or preserve a fine integer lattice inside the continuous normalization blocks.

## 6. Explicit component-indicator calibration

For P={0,1}^2, all four components are singletons and L(P) is all functions on P. Take G(z)=z_1 z_2. The exact component indicators are

    chi_00=1-z_1-z_2+G,
    chi_10=z_1-G,
    chi_01=z_2-G,
    chi_11=G.

This checks why a single continuous feature accommodates all four component-dependent offsets and isolates their cuts even though those offsets need not be affine in the original base alone. With m-dimensional full fibers the lift has continuous dimension 4m+1 and full total dimension 4m+3, while every integer fiber remains intrinsically m-dimensional.

The accompanying Fraction verifier checks these identities, a non-affine offset representation, common determinant normalization on crossing rectangles, the induced intrinsic volumes, and the full affine span for four m=2 block fibers. These finite checks calibrate the formulas; the proofs above establish the general claims.

## 7. File-specific final audit of the saved theorem

The final source `candidate c344f12be982dcb7` has now been read in full and **PASSES**. Its normalization takes M_l to be exactly the retained total, so the main theorem has total intrinsic mass one; the discarded-mass factor appears separately and correctly in Section 6.

The additional bound ell<=h(P)<=2^k is valid. The representation graph preserves convexly closed traces in both directions, hence its finite Helly number. Choosing ell affinely independent graph points and the ell closed facets of their simplex gives an infeasible family with every ell-1 subfamily containing a selected graph vertex. Other graph points do not matter because all facets already have empty geometric intersection. At ell=1 the one-member empty-set family gives the required lower bound. Doignon applied with conv(P) proves the upper bound even if that auxiliary set is selected: removing it still leaves a family whose intersection misses P. At k=0, P is one point, h(P)=ell=s=1, and D=m exactly.

Its Section 5 correctly separates the entire-component restriction from proper component cuts. When there is only one component, that entire-component case is simply the trivial mass-one upper bound; no proper halfspace representation of the whole ambient space is needed. The actual depth infimum is supplied by the proper cuts, while adding an artificial mass-one candidate does not change it. Thus the stated exact isolation and maximum-depth convergence remain valid also at s=1 and k=0.

All dimension bounds, common fiber Jacobians, finite-measure normalization, closed supporting boundaries, and the stated fine-lattice limitation agree with the independent proof above. No correction to the saved theorem is required.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
